item.title: Missteps Mount in Justice Dept.’s Case Against Minnesota Anti-ICE Protesters
item.description: The problems plaguing the case have not only hurt the government’s chances, lawyers say, but have also undermined the bonds of trust that prosecutors have traditionally enjoyed in court.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Ernesto Londoño
item.media:description: Nekima Levy Armstrong, center, a local civil rights lawyer, is a lead defendant in the Justice Department’s case against a group of activists and journalists who were arrested over a demonstration at a St. Paul, Minn., church.

item.title: G.O.P. Kills Bid to Expand I.V.F. Access in the Military
item.description: In a notable shift, Republican senators voted unanimously against a proposal to expand the military’s coverage of fertility treatments.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Senator Tammy Duckworth, Democrat of Illinois, offered the provision for the defense bill that would have broadened the availability of in vitro fertilization for members of the military.

item.title: Texas and Florida Draw Up Terrorism Lists and Take Aim at a Muslim Group
item.description: The federal government designates terrorism groups. But Governors Ron DeSantis and Greg Abbott have gotten in the game, and a focus is CAIR, a nonprofit.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Council on American Islamic Relations in Washington.

item.title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson

item.title: What Is the Board of Peace? The Trump-Backed Group, Explained.
item.description: President Trump created the international organization, aimed at resolving the long-running war in Gaza and other conflicts.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: President Trump at a signing ceremony for the founding charter of the Board of Peace at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January.

item.title: Kennedy Center Halts Free Public Tours After Five Decades of Service
item.description: The decision to suspend tours came after a volunteer tour guide was featured in a Times article detailing President Trump’s dramatic revamp of the Kennedy Center.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Williamson
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Jared Soares for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Kennedy Center in Washington in June. It has now ended free public tours of the facility.

item.title: Defying Trump, Cornyn Uses His Lame-Duck Power
item.description: In standing in the way of Todd Blanche, President Trump’s choice for attorney general, a liberated Senator John Cornyn is wielding his leverage.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: Senator John Cornyn in Washington, on Thursday.

item.title: Trump Says Peace Board Has Plan for Gaza Disarmament
item.description: There was no immediate comment from Hamas or Israel, though the Board of Peace said Hamas had agreed to a “road map” to give up its weapons.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers and Pranav Baskar
item.media:description: President Trump at the Board of Peace charter announcement at the World Economic Forum, in Davos, Switzerland, in January.

item.title: Alabama Plans Inmate’s Execution After Supreme Court Blocked Last Attempt
item.description: The state will try again to execute Jeffery Lee — this time, by lethal injection — after courts said doing so using nitrogen gas was “likely unconstitutional.”
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas
item.media:description: Alabama’s lethal injection chamber at the Holman Correctional Facility in Atmore, Ala., around 2002.

item.title: Seattle’s Police Chief Resigns Under Pressure After Festival Shooting
item.description: The decision followed days of criticism over how the department handled the release of information about a shooting that killed three people.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:description: Chief Shon Barnes of the Seattle Police Department at a vigil for victims of a shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival.

item.title: Texas Parents Try New Tactic to Remove Ten Commandments From Schools
item.description: A lawsuit filed by three parents argues that the displays violate a state religious freedom law and asks for them to be removed before school starts in August.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman
item.media:credit: Desiree Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Ten Commandments poster displayed in a classroom in Fort Worth, Texas.

item.title: Two More Appeals Courts Rule Against Trump’s Detention Policy
item.description: The rulings deepen a split across the judiciary, making it more likely that the Supreme Court will consider the legality of detaining undocumented immigrants indefinitely.
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:credit: Paul Ratje for The New York Times
item.media:description: Large tents meant to house thousands of immigrant detainees at Camp East Montana, a detention facility built at Fort Bliss in El Paso.

item.title: Dulles Airport’s Reviled ‘People Movers’ May Be Lurching Into the Sunset
item.description: A $22.5 billion redesign plan eliminates the “mobile lounges,” which were conceived as a way of making air travel more efficient. Many passengers found the opposite to be true.
item.dc:creator: Sopan Deb
item.media:description: A mobile lounge at Dulles International Airport in Northern Virginia last year.

item.title: T.S.A. Finds 5 Civil War Cannonballs in Passenger’s Luggage in Alabama
item.description: The inert relics, some as big as a grapefruit, were detected when agents X-rayed checked bags.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro

item.title: Does Congress Have the Power to Stop the Iran War?
item.description: In theory, the War Powers Act gives Congress the power to end a war. But our chief White House correspondent, Peter Baker, describes how President Trump is the latest president to find ways to engage in war without congressional approval.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker, Paul Abowd, Thomas Vollkommer, Jon Hazell, Jon Miller, Ray Whitehouse, Stephanie Swart and Rafaela Balster
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Trump’s Nominee to Oversee VOA, Sarah B. Rogers, Suggests Return of Journalists on Leave
item.description: The statement by the nominee, Sarah B. Rogers, signaled a stark reversal of the president’s earlier efforts to shutter Voice of America and other federally funded news groups.
item.dc:creator: Minho Kim
item.category: United States Agency for Global Media
item.media:description: During a confirmation hearing on Thursday, Sarah B. Rogers, President Trump’s nominee to lead the parent organization of Voice of America, suggested she would reinstate many of the journalists who had been placed on paid leave after an executive order effectively dismantled the organization last year.

item.title: Trump’s Effort to Gut Education Dept. Rebuked by Senate Committee
item.description: The bipartisan bill is a long way from becoming law, but it represents the strongest opposition yet from Congress to the administration’s agenda.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Michael A. McCoy for The New York Times
item.media:description: The vote represented the sharpest opposition from Congress over the administration’s attempt to eliminate the Education Department.

item.title: Former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes Exits Race for Wisconsin Governor
item.description: With a democratic socialist, Francesca Hong, leading in polls, former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes said he was ending his campaign in the closely divided state.
item.dc:creator: Mitch Smith and Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mandela Barnes, a former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, in Madison in June.

item.title: U.S. Government Mislabels Map of African Countries at AIDS Conference

item.title: Colin Gray, Father of Teenage Shooter in Georgia, Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison
item.description: Prosecutors argued that Colin Gray bore responsibility for the 2024 shooting because he had given his son a gun and failed to act as the teen’s mental health deteriorated.

item.title: Why Democrats Won’t Stop Forcing Votes On Trump’s Iran War Powers
item.description: Even after winning approval of a measure calling on President Trump to end the war, they continue to call votes to force Republicans to answer for it.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Democrat of New York, put forward this week the latest measure to rein in the president’s war powers.

item.title: Elon Musk Plans at Least $100 Million in Midterm Spending to Help Republicans
item.description: Elon Musk, a year after a huge blowup with President Trump and the Republican Party, is said to be planning to spend in at least eight states to help them in November.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Jim Vondruska for The New York Times
item.media:description: Elon Musk was the biggest donor in the 2024 presidential election, when he spent hundreds of millions.

item.title: Bipartisan Senate Bill Would Give Judiciary Control of Some Courthouses
item.description: A new bipartisan bill comes after years of complaints from the courts that the General Services Administration is a bad landlord.
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:description: Senator Richard J. Durbin, Democrat of Illinois and the lead sponsor of a new bipartisan bill, said the purpose of the proposed law was to “ensure our federal courthouses remain safe, secure and operating effectively for those who work in and visit them.”

item.title: Trump Threatens to Withdraw Blanche as Attorney General, Dealing Blow to Nomination
item.description: President Trump’s threat followed a day of fruitless negotiations with two Republican holdouts, Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush, Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:description: The two senators object to a deal negotiated by Todd Blanche and President Trump’s personal lawyers to resolve a lawsuit the president had filed against the I.R.S.
